obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (merchant and service provider)
citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: Merchant: the acquirer agreement requires an annual ROC by a QSA for the owned and leased hotels' merchant accounts, and the company operates the payment systems at the 72 managed hotels under the management agreements. Service provider: the CRS stores guarantee card data for franchised hotels and SL-2 clients, and the company administers the PMS tenant, the tokenization service and the managed property network for franchisees, so the service-provider-only requirements apply. Card brand level thresholds were not verified from a card brand primary source

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: For-profit company; no size threshold. Deception for security, privacy, loyalty and pricing statements; unfairness for unreasonable security, including systems the company designs, connects or manages for franchisees (FTC v. Wyndham Worldwide Corp., 799 F.3d 236 (3d Cir. 2015)). Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (analyzed under N72-R02)
basis: The company offers short-term lodging (464.1) and charges mandatory resort and destination fees at resort collection and urban hotels, displayed on its website, app, chatbot, microsites, channel feeds and contact center

obligation: FTC Disposal Rule
basis: The company obtains background-check reports on applicants from a consumer reporting agency

obligation: State breach notification laws
citation: State statutes in each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Guest, member and employee personal information from residents of every state; hotels in 33 states and DC; counsel's state matrix. Florida is the worked example

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: 118 Florida hotels and Florida guests' personal information, including identity document numbers

obligation: Florida guest register
basis: 118 Florida hotels keep an electronic guest register in the PMS

obligation: Florida price gouging during declared emergencies (worked example)
basis: The statute names dwelling units and essential commodities rather than hotels expressly; the company treats room rates as covered. Other states' laws are handled the same way

obligation: CCPA and its cybersecurity audit regulations
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; 11 CCR 7120-7124
basis: California hotels and guests; revenue above the CCPA threshold of $26,625,000; personal information of more than 250,000 consumers (about 61 million guest profiles)

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: Revenue exceeds $1 billion, but the company does not earn 50% or more of revenue from online advertising, operate a consumer smart speaker and voice command service, or operate an app store with at least 250,000 applications, so it is not a controller

obligation: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act
basis: No biometric identifiers are collected at the Illinois hotels: time clocks are badge-based and mobile check-in face matching is disabled there. The statute text was not re-verified

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed)
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as pending. The proposed size criterion would cover the company because it exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 721110. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over ERP, payroll, and owner and franchise fee accounting are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a HIPAA covered entity: it is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule and Red Flags Rule
basis: The company extends no consumer credit; the co-brand credit card is issued by a bank

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom or extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts in the contract repository; government travelers book like any guest

obligation: Acquirer agreement and card brand rules
citation: Acquirer agreement (fictional terms); card brand operating rules
basis: The acquirer agreement requires an annual QSA ROC and notice within 24 hours of a suspected compromise; card brand rules apply through it

obligation: Management and franchise agreements and brand technology standards
citation: Management agreements; franchise agreements; BS-TECH-01 to BS-TECH-06 (fictional terms)
basis: Owner notice within 24 hours under management agreements; 72-hour notice and PCI DSS acknowledgment in franchise agreements since 2022 (212 earlier agreements lack them); franchisees report to the brand within 24 hours under BS-TECH-06

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 client commitments
citation: Franchise technology services terms; SL-2 client agreements
basis: SL-1 franchisees receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report; SL-2 agreements set 99.9% availability and 4-hour recovery, and two management companies require a SOC 2 Type 2 report

obligation: Sherman Act Section 1 (algorithmic pricing)
basis: The revenue-management contract pools non-public rate and occupancy data from the company's hotels and 212 independently owned franchised hotels; analyzed as litigation risk, not a compliance checklist

obligation: State laws on AI in employment decisions
applies: Yes, for AI-006 at the Illinois and California hotels
basis: The applicant ranking feature was switched on at 22 hotels, including 2 in Illinois and 3 in California
